content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Dispatchers and Background Execution** as part of **Coroutines, Asynchronous Programming, and Concurrency**. A coroutine can suspend without blocking the thread, but it still runs on threads; scope lifetime, dispatcher choice, cancellation, and shared state remain important. Use the subtopics—Main, Default, and I/O Dispatchers, Selecting the Appropriate Dispatcher, Avoiding Blocking Work on Inappropriate Threads—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous code introduces lifecycle, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Structured concurrency and explicit data flow make these concerns easier to reason about.
